title: Instrumented local-loop lightning onramp (quick run notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, instrumented quickstart for devs who want to go from zero to an observable SDK integration in ~15 minutes. Focus: local-first flow (node + python examples), baseline telemetry events, smoke assertions, and clear first-responder steps when things go wrong.

Audience:
- Developer advocates and SDK maintainers running demos
- Integrator engineers who need a reproducible local loop for chat + embedding use cases

Goals (what this quickstart achieves):
1) App runs locally calling Redwood-hosted sandbox model with a single env var.
2) Telemetry emits three required signals: request.start, request.finish, and token.delta (approx).
3) Basic smoke tests validate latency < 500ms for short prompts and successful embeddings generation.
4) Troubleshooting checklist to recover from common errors without filing an SRE ticket.

Prereqs (tiny):
- Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed
- Redwood API key (sandbox) available in REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Git + curl for quick checks

Quick install (pick one)
Node (one-liner):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples && cd sdk-samples/lightning-onramp
2) npm ci
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_sandbox_xxx
4) npm run start:node  # starts express demo + telemetry forwarder

Python (one-liner):
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples && cd sdk-samples/lightning-onramp/python
2) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
3) pip install -r requirements.txt
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_sandbox_xxx
5) python app.py  # starts flask demo + local instrumenter

What the app does (minimal):
- Accepts a prompt in a tiny web UI or curl endpoint /generate
- Calls Redwood text generation API with streaming disabled (first pass)
- Emits telemetry to stdout and optional local file (telemetry.jsonl) with our required signal set

Required telemetry schema (informal):
- event: request.start
  - fields: timestamp_iso, request_id, user_agent, route, model, prompt_length
- event: request.finish
  - fields: timestamp_iso, request_id, status_code, latency_ms, tokens_out_est
- event: token.delta (aggregated every 50 tokens or at finish)
  - fields: timestamp_iso, request_id, tokens_emitted

These are intentionally lightweight: we don't ship proto yet, just JSONL to make demos reproducible.

Smoke tests (local):
- curl -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello world"}'
  Expect: 200 JSON with text field and telemetry.log contains request.finish for same request_id
- embeddings check:
  curl -X POST localhost:8080/embeddings -d '{"input":"redwood"}'
  Expect: 200 JSON with vector length 1536 (or model-specific) and telemetry token.delta entry present

Sample minimal JS request (for copy-paste in README):
const res = await fetch(process.env.BACKEND + '/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'What is Redwood?' }) });
const j = await res.json();
console.log(j.text);

Common failure modes + first actions:
1) 401 / invalid key
   - Check REDWOOD_API_KEY set and not expired; run curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
   - If still 401, try sandbox key from GH PR linked above or rotate in Console
2) request hangs (no request.finish)
   - Check network (proxy/env) and confirm streaming flag in demo is false
   - Look for server-side stack in logs; restart process and reproduce
3) telemetry missing or malformed
   - Confirm local file writable (permissions), check JSONL newline delimited formatting (jq . will error if broken)
   - If telemetry not present at all, ensure start script includes --emit-telemetry flag
4) embeddings return empty vector or different dims
   - Confirm model selection in demo config (default: embed-small-v1) and update sample assert

Gating for handing the demo to Solutions / customer-facing kit:
- Must pass smoke tests on macOS and Ubuntu runners
- Telemetry fields present for 100 consecutive requests in CI run (simple loop)
- README contains one-line repro for both Node and Python

CI sanity job (sketch):
- checkout, install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY from secrets
- run demo in background
- run 20 quick curl requests and assert every response contains text and telemetry lines
- if any fail, collect logs and attach to GH PR

Observability checklist (what we look at locally):
- In telemetry.jsonl: 1 request.start and 1 request.finish per request_id
- request.finish.latency_ms mean < 500ms for short prompts (on sandbox)
- No more than 2% 5xx responses in a run of 200 requests (should be 0 in demo)
- Token.delta counts sum roughly to tokens_out_est in finish event (fuzzy match)

UX quicknotes for demos (voice):
- Keep the UI tiny: single prompt, single result, copy button for output
- Show a tiny status badge: "Connected to sandbox (latency: X ms)"
- Expose a toggle: "emit-telemetry (on/off)" so demos can show the JSONL streaming live

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we adopt structured schema (proto) now or keep JSONL for fast iteration? (ask Eng-Observability)
- Add a streaming demo branch: how to represent partial token.delta events safely in demo UI?
- Replace hardcoded model names with discovery from the hosted catalog API? quick RFC: ENG-5470
- Add a step to exercise rollouts/fallbacks (dedicated -> hosted) for resilience story

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Could add a tiny lambda in examples that validates telemetry and posts a badge to PR (good CI signal)
- Consider embedding a simple cost meter (tokens * model_unit_cost) in the UI for teachable demo on economics

Links referenced during prototyping:
- GH PR with sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pull/212
- Console quickstart for sandbox keys (internal): confluence:ENG/onboarding/sandbox-keys (placeholder)
- Slack thread: #devexp-lightning-onramp (see pinned messages)

If you run this and hit any ambiguity ping @elena or @sasha in Slack. I'll iterate this into a one-page README and a tiny screencast as next steps.

End of quick notes (draft).
